message: _decode_token falls back to jwt.decode with verify_signature=False and algorithms ['HS256','none'], so any unsigned/unsigned-'none' token is accepted and full authentication is bypassed.
JWT tokens verified with hardcoded key 'secret' instead of the configured SECRET_KEY; attacker can forge valid tokens.
Flask SECRET_KEY hardcoded to 'supersecret' in source (also duplicated in docker-compose.yml), enabling session/signature forgery.
Any Origin header is reflected into Access-Control-Allow-Origin together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, letting any site make credentialed cross-origin requests.
app.run(host='0.0.0.0', debug=True) exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger (remote code execution) on all interfaces.
Passwords hashed/verified with unsalted MD5; trivially rainbow-tabled/cracked, no key stretching.
register() interpolates user-supplied username into an f-string INSERT executed via db.session.execute - classic SQL injection.
login() interpolates username into an f-string SELECT - SQL injection against the user table.
Login JWT signed with hardcoded key 'secret'; token forgery for any user_id.
session_token cookie set with httponly=False and secure=False, exposing the auth token to JavaScript (XSS) and to unencrypted transport.
update-password lets any authenticated user change the password of any other user by supplying a user_id, with no old-password verification - full account takeover of arbitrary accounts.
Reset token is deterministic md5(username) with no expiry; anyone who knows the username can compute a valid reset token and take over the account.
forgot-password returns the reset token itself in the 'debug_token' response field, hand-delivering a valid account-takeover token to the caller.
yaml.load with Loader=yaml.Loader (full loader) on user-supplied YAML allows arbitrary Python object construction -> remote code execution.
get_transactions interpolates the user_id query param (a raw string) into an f-string SQL query - SQL injection.
Any authenticated user can pass an arbitrary user_id to read another user's transaction history.
search_transactions interpolates the description search term into a LIKE clause inside an f-string SQL query - SQL injection.
Transfer amount is never validated as positive or bounded; a negative amount increases the sender's balance (self-transfer prints money) / drains the receiver.

quickpay debits current_user.balance with no sufficiency or sign check (unlike /api/transfer), allowing negative balances and negative-amount money creation; also relies on a non-HttpOnly cookie auth path.
split-bill accepts a client-controlled from_user_id and debits that user's balance, letting any authenticated user move funds out of any other account (no payer auth, no balance check).
transaction_receipt has no auth decorator at all; any unauthenticated party can read arbitrary transaction details by id.
Receipt HTML template interpolates attacker-controlled transaction.description (and sender/receiver names) unescaped into an HTML document.
Upload filename is taken verbatim from the client and joined to UPLOAD_DIR (with os.makedirs on the attacker-controlled dirname), allowing writes outside the upload dir, e.g. '../../' overwrites.
serve_upload joins <path:filename> to UPLOAD_DIR without normalization; the isfile() check is bypassed by '../' sequences, enabling arbitrary file read (unauthenticated).
Production credentials committed in source: live API key, AWS access/secret keys, Stripe key, database password, SendGrid key, GitHub token, JWT private key, Slack webhook.
generate_report passes user-controlled report_type/date_range into a shell=True subprocess via f-string - arbitrary command execution.
system_status passes the service query param directly into os.popen(f"systemctl status {service}") - shell command injection.
ping_host runs f"ping -c 3 {host}" with shell=True on user input - arbitrary command execution.
dns_lookup runs f"nslookup {domain}" with shell=True on user input - arbitrary command execution.
webhook-test fetches a fully user-supplied URL (requests.get) with no scheme/host restrictions and returns the response body - server-side request forgery (cloud metadata, internal services).
fetch-avatar requests a user-supplied URL with verify=False - SSRF plus disabled certificate validation; response exfiltrated as base64.
download_statement sends os.path.join('/app/statements/', filename) with an unvalidated filename; '../' sequences read arbitrary files.
view_log opens /var/log/{file} with a raw user-supplied file name; '../' traversal reads arbitrary files such as /etc/passwd.
lxml parser configured with resolve_entities=True and no_network=False on user-supplied XML; DOCTYPE external entities enable file disclosure and SSRF (lxml can execute external entities).
import-session base64-decodes user input and calls pickle.loads on it - arbitrary code execution via a crafted pickle payload.
update_user applies every JSON field via setattr(user, key), so any caller can set role='admin' (or balance, reset_token, password_hash) on any user.
preview_email renders the user-supplied template string with Jinja render_template_string - SSTI leads to RCE (e.g. {{config}}/{{request.application...}}).
/api/redirect sends a 302 to an unvalidated, user-supplied url parameter (unauthenticated open redirect usable for phishing).
Admin endpoints (list_all_users and the whole admin blueprint) only require a valid token; no role=='admin' check, so any regular user can invoke admin APIs.
list_all_users returns every user's password_hash and full profile (SSN, DOB, address) to any authenticated client.
re.match is run with a fully user-controlled regex pattern over usernames - denial of service via catastrophic backtracking patterns.
calculate() calls eval() on a user-supplied expression string - arbitrary Python code execution.
run-script() calls exec() on a user-supplied script string - arbitrary Python code execution.
format-data() compiles then exec()s a user-supplied format string - arbitrary Python code execution.
Hardcoded master admin password 'MasterAdmin@2024!' compared in source; anyone who finds it gets the admin flag.
Authorization enforced with assert(), which is stripped under python -O, silently removing the admin-only guard.
dashboard-data returns the hardcoded ADMIN_API_KEY and AWS access key in the JSON response to any authenticated user.
JWT auth token persisted in localStorage, readable by any injected script (combined with the app's XSS sinks this yields full session theft).
handleCalculate runs eval() on a user-typed expression in the browser - arbitrary JS execution in the admin's session.
A window 'message' listener evals data.payload from any origin with no event.origin check - any web page can execute JS in the admin panel.
searchHtml is built by string-interpolating the raw, unescaped search query (line 37) and injected via dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
The ?notes= URL parameter is rendered unescaped via dangerouslySetInnerHTML - trivial reflected XSS (e.g. for admin links in phishing).
renderAnnouncement concatenates unescaped user text into container.innerHTML, executing any HTML/script the admin or a spoofed input posts.
Hardcoded 'admin_master_key_2024' written to localStorage as a session secret alongside fabricated admin permission flags.
Pins known-vulnerable versions: Werkzeug 2.0.1 (CVE-2023-46136 debugger RCE), Flask 2.0.1 (CVE-2023-30861 cookie injection), PyJWT 2.1.0, PyYAML 5.3.1 (unsafe yaml.load).
